messages:
Nate: quick follow-up from the hotstart RFC: i want to propose a lightweight \"warmup transaction\" (wtx) concept to make manifestless shard rollouts atomic for readers. goal: avoid partial-hotstart races where some nodes serve new shards and others still use old ones.

Sanjay: curious how this differs from a manifest file that becomes visible only after upload? main pain is race between prefetch and activation.

Nate: difference is we make a tiny \"commit object\" that contains shard list + checksums + state. prefetchers can start fetching when state=announced, but runtime only activates shards when state=committed. so upload path: upload shards -> create wtx(state=announced) -> background verify -> flip to committed.

Mia: extra object store ops per rollout. are we okay with per-canary overhead?

Devon: overhead negligible compared to model blobs. bigger concern: verify latency could add tail latency to canary flips. we should allow a soft-commit mode for canaries (treat announced as committed for specific canary pools).

Nate: yes, rollout plan: phase1=announce-only (prefetch allowed, no activation), phase2=verify (background checksums/compat), phase3=commit (activate). on verify timeout -> wtx.state=failed -> prefetch eviction.

Olivia: security: wtx must be signed. for hosted we can use internal signing key; for Dedicated/Private we require KMS/HSM signature so someone can't flip wtx to point at malicious shards.

Sanjay: runtime eviction rules? prefetchers must not leave cache entries forever if commit never happens. propose default TTL 1h and immediate purge on wtx.failed.

Mia: what about older agents that don't understand wtx? backward compatibility is tricky. maybe we support opt-in enforcement: feature-flag per deployment so older nodes continue to activate on shard presence.

Devon: metrics we need: wtx_verify_latency, wtx_commit_time, wtx_verify_fail_rate, wtx_active_count. add traces for shard->wtx mapping to debug partial rollouts.

Nate: sketch wtx schema (just a small object):
```json
{"wtxid":"wtx-1799070000-01","model":"resnet-llm-v1","shards":["s3://.../m-000.safetensors","s3://.../m-001.safetensors"],"state":"announced|verifying|committed|failed","signed_by":"kms:key-123","issued_at":"1799070000"}
```

Sanjay: that JSON is fine as a schema example but runtime needs to record per-shard checksum too. otherwise verification is weak.

Nate: agree, we'll include per-shard sha256 in final RFC.

Mia: Private/onprem note: objectstore semantics differ (NFS, GCS, local disk). allow pluggable signer + different visibility checks. also add migration doc for agents <v0.9.

Devon: tests: simulate commit failing mid-rollout, simulate verify delayed so some nodes see shards by path, others don't. ensure eviction playbook recovers gracefully.

Olivia: security will review KMS signing + audit logs. also recommend timestamp + replay-protection on wtx to avoid rollback attacks.

InfraBot: deploybot: starting wtx-canary job for eng-ml-canary, id=wtx-1799070000-01 :rocket:

Mia: i'll write the RFC addendum with schema, TTL defaults, three-phase rollout, backward compatibility plan, and the metrics table. assigning to me.

Nate: i'll add the runtime change list: prefetch semantics (announce-only), activation gating (commit only), eviction rules, and test checklist.

Sanjay: i'll draft an ops rollback playbook and add instructions for forced-commit if verify erroneously times out for critical outages.

Devon: +1 let's include a short benchmark: canary commit latency observed ~200-600ms for metadata ops in our test S3, verify depends mostly on shard size but checksum streaming adds ~1-2s per GB.

Olivia: noted. security will schedule a quick review this week.

Mia: ack. :thumbsup:
